Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: customer-service-reply
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle is a legitimate template generator for customer service responses. The core logic in `scripts/cs.sh` is a Python script that provides static text templates for various scenarios (pre-sale, complaints, refunds, etc.) based on command-line arguments. It does not perform any network requests, file system modifications, or sensitive data access, and it lacks any signs of obfuscation or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill is self-contained and matches its stated purpose (generating customer-service templates), but a static scan detected unicode control characters in the SKILL.md which could hide prompt-injection or other unexpected content — inspect the files before installing or running.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (generate customer-service reply templates) and the included script is local and readable. However, the static scan found unicode control characters in SKILL.md which can hide content or prompt-injection payloads. Before installing or running: 1) Open SKILL.md and scripts/cs.sh in an editor that shows invisible characters or inspect with hexdump -C / od -c / cat -v to reveal control bytes. 2) Review the full cs.sh (ensure the truncated portion contains no network calls like curl/wget/nc, no subprocess exec that invokes remote code, and no reading of sensitive files). 3) Run the script in an isolated environment (container or VM) first. 4) Optionally run static checks (shellcheck) and scan for suspicious commands (curl, wget, nc, ssh, scp, python imports of subprocess/os.system, open(...) of ~/.ssh or /etc). If you find hidden control characters or unexpected network/credential access in the rest of the files, do not install. If you want, provide the full untruncated cs.sh and the raw SKILL.md bytes and I can re-check them — that would raise my confidence.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: The SKILL.md contained unicode control characters flagged by the scanner. For a simple template generator this is unexpected — such characters can be used to hide instructions or influence prompt parsing. This finding warrants manual inspection of the raw file (including invisible characters).
